speaker: Doctor
text: To better understand your chronic joint pain, can you describe exactly where it hurts and what activities make it worse or better? Additionally, have you noticed any morning stiffness or visible swelling in the affected areas?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description; the pattern of pain worsening with activity and improving with rest in your knees and hips is very suggestive of osteoarthritis, but the involvement of your great toe is unusual for this condition. Has the pain in your great toe ever been associated with sudden, severe redness, swelling, and tenderness, as if it were a stone in the shoe? Also, have you noticed any lumps or bony overgrowths on your joints?
